name: Familial Anetoderma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Histopathological Diagnostic Criteria for Familial Anetoderma

criteria.description: Presence of multiple well-circumscribed, flaccid, sac-like skin lesions with localized areas of slack skin
Histopathological confirmation showing focal loss or fragmentation of elastic fibers in the dermis
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance pattern
Lack of significant inflammatory infiltrate in skin biopsy
Preserved collagen fibers on histology differentiating from other connective tissue disorders

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic clinical lesions plus histopathological evidence of elastic fiber loss
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but is not routinely available

laboratory: Negative autoimmune serologies in most cases
genetic: No specific gene identified; genetic testing not routinely available
other: Histopathology showing focal loss or fragmentation of elastic fibers in dermis
Special stains (e.g., Verhoeff-Van Gieson) confirm elastin loss

distinguishingFeatures: Often associated with autoimmune or infectious diseases
Systemic involvement including cardiovascular and ophthalmological manifestations
Histopathology shows calcification of elastic fibers
Diffuse fine wrinkling rather than localized sac-like lesions
Histology shows mid-dermal elastin loss without familial pattern

redFlags: Development of systemic symptoms such as cardiovascular or ocular abnormalities
Signs of secondary infection or ulceration at lesion sites
references: Bolognia JL, Schaffer JV, Cerroni L. Dermatology. 4th ed. Elsevier; 2018.
Hashimoto K, et al. Familial anetoderma: clinical and histopathological study. J Dermatol. 2015.
